topic: why raising the source level cannot lift coherence
method: same cross-spectrum estimator on two capture sets; quiet set = -18 dBFS nominal (2 captures), loud set = -6 dBFS nominal (6 captures); 2048-point Hann, 50% overlap

interpretation.if_interference_were_additive_electrical: a 12 dB source increase should yield 12 dB of SNR gain and coherence near 1
interpretation.observed: only about 4-9 dB of SNR gain, so roughly half of the interfering energy scales with the source
interpretation.therefore: the unpredictable part is dominated by acoustic reverberation whose tail exceeds the 512-tap memory (10.5 ms), not by an analogue noise floor

consequences.coherence_0.8_unreachable_by_level: at 4-8 kHz the SNR is about +2.4 dB and one dB of level buys about 0.4 dB of SNR, so reaching +6 dB needs roughly 9 dB more level; only 6 dB remain between -6 and 0 dBFS
consequences.supports_longer_memory: the missing energy is real acoustic tail beyond 10.5 ms, which is exactly what a longer-memory model would capture
consequences.measurement_method: noise correlation is the wrong estimator in a reverberant field; a log sweep with inverse-filter deconvolution recovers the impulse response without relying on coherence

status: measurement not yet adequate for model fitting; no model and no cancellation target is claimed from these captures
board_state: unreachable at the time of writing; the multi-band loud run stopped after 2 of 8 bands
